newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour calls for fast Euro gas liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour calls for fast Euro gas liberalisation.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party on Tuesday urged the U.K. government to make progress towards the liberalisation of the European gas market at today's European Union Energy Council meeting in Brussels.
"U.K. gas and electricity companies should have the same right to compete in Europe as European companies have here," John Battle, Labour's spokesman for energy and industry, said in a statement.
European energy ministers were meeting in Brussels on Tuesday to discuss the amended proposal for an EU directive on opening up the European natural gas market.
The meeting will be the first since the issue was put on hold two years ago when the freeing up of the electricity market was given priority.
Last week, U.K. energy minister Lord Fraser pledged to keep the pressure on its EU partners to bring about gas liberalisation, but admitted that the path faced hurdles and reluctant members.
After six years of wrangling, EU members reached agreement in June on a limited opening of electricity markets.
"We now need to do the same thing for gas...(but) I appreciate that there are concerns about this change of direction," Lord Fraser told a conference in London.
Britain, the Netherlands and Germany are the most in favour of gas liberalisation, while France and Belgium have adopted a more sceptical attitude.
"The creation of a single market in energy is a crucial step forward for Britain in Europe," said Labour's Battle.
"The liberalisation of our own internal markets, welcome in itself, has allowed European competitors to win market share in gas without British firms having the right to compete in Europe."
